about: Eletrobras is Brazil's largest electricity generation and transmission company, operating hydro, nuclear (via Eletronuclear), wind and solar plants plus tens of thousands of kilometres of transmission lines. It was privatised in 2022 when the federal government reduced its stake, and is listed on the B3 exchange (ELET3, ELET6) and NYSE (EBR), headquartered in Rio de Janeiro. Sells power to distributors and large industry. B2B, though a well known name in Brazil.

Inkia Energy operates and develops power generation, per Crunchbase, and is based in Lima, Peru, in the electronics and power grid categories. It was a Latin American and Caribbean power generation and distribution group, historically owned by Israel Corporation (Kenon Holdings) before later sales of its assets. Crunchbase shows about $1.7 billion in funding. B2B power producer with minimal consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Mainstream Renewable Power is a wind and solar developer founded in 2008 by Eddie O'Connor, now headquartered in Norway after Aker Horizons took a majority stake, with projects in Chile, South Africa, Ireland, the US and offshore wind in the UK and Ireland. Customers are utilities and corporate buyers. Ownership has changed amid Aker Horizons' restructuring. Crunchbase shows about $2.1 billion in funding. B2B renewables developer, no consumer brand.

Crunchbase shows about $1.15 billion in funding. B2B energy asset manager serving homeowners via third parties; low direct consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Superior Energy Services is a Houston, Texas oilfield services provider supplying specialised tools and well intervention, drilling support and rental equipment to oil and gas operators, historically working onshore and offshore worldwide. It restructured under bankruptcy in 2020 and emerged as a private company, later delisted. Founded in 1989, it focuses on specialty tools and services. Funding shown is about $775 million. It is a B2B business with little consumer brand awareness.

about: Clarios is a global maker of automotive batteries, headquartered in Glendale, Wisconsin (Milwaukee area), spun out of Johnson Controls in 2019 and owned by Brookfield Business Partners. It supplies roughly one in three of the world's cars with 12-volt and start-stop batteries, and sells the brands Varta, Optima, LTH and Interstate under OEM supply deals. It operates dozens of plants worldwide and has revenue near 9 billion dollars. Brands like Varta and Optima are visible to aftermarket consumers.

CNNC Huineng is the clean-energy arm of China National Nuclear Corporation, focused on developing, building and operating wind, solar and other renewable energy projects. It is based in Beijing (Fengtai) and is a state-owned subsidiary. Funding shown is about 8.29 million yuan. Customers are grid companies. B2B state-owned business with no consumer visibility.

about: Qcells is the US arm of Hanwha Qcells, a South Korean solar manufacturer, developing and building solar modules, storage and projects, including a large panel factory in Georgia, and a residential solar sales and installation arm. It is a Hanwha Solutions unit; Hanwha Solutions is listed in Seoul. US operations are headquartered in Irvine, California. Customers are installers, utilities and homeowners. Strong brand in solar, with some sports sponsorships.

wiki.title: Qcells
wiki.text: Qcells is a manufacturer of photovoltaic cells. The company is headquartered in Seoul, South Korea, after being founded in 1999 in Bitterfeld-Wolfen, Germany, where the company still has its engineering offices. Qcells was purchased out of bankruptcy in August 2012 by the Hanwha Group, a South Korean business conglomerate. Qcells now operates as a subsidiary of Hanwha Solutions, the group's energy and petrochemical company.

about: Suniva is a US manufacturer of crystalline silicon photovoltaic solar cells, based in Norcross, Georgia, which filed for bankruptcy in 2017 and brought the Section 201 solar trade case that led to US tariffs on imported panels. It later emerged from bankruptcy under new ownership. Customers are US module makers and installers. B2B with minimal consumer visibility.

about: Solaris, formerly Solarisbank, is a Berlin-based banking-as-a-service and embedded finance platform, offering a licensed bank, cards, lending, accounts and compliance to fintechs, retailers and brands that want to offer financial products. Founded in 2016, it raised funding from SBI, Santander, Visa and others, and later restructured in 2024 under SBI Group control. B2B and known in the fintech sector, not to consumers.

APR Energy is a US-based provider of fast-track mobile gas turbine power plants, supplying temporary and bridging electricity to utilities, governments and industry in countries such as Iraq, Argentina, Libya and the Americas. Based in Jacksonville, Florida. It is privately held. Revenue is rental and fuel. B2B with no consumer profile.

Lunar Energy is a US residential energy storage and software company, founded in 2022 by Kunal Girotra (former Tesla Powerwall leader) and Kevin Doran, offering Lunar System home batteries and Gridshare software that aggregates batteries into virtual power plants. Based in Mountain View, California, it acquired Moixa from the UK in 2022 and is backed by Sequoia-linked, Mitsubishi, Celesta and others. Sells to homeowners via installers. Young brand with modest consumer awareness.

about: AMPYR Distributed Energy is a London-headquartered developer and owner of distributed renewable energy, designing, building and operating on-site solar, battery storage and microgrids for commercial and industrial customers and community projects across Europe, Australia and the US. It is a platform of the AMPYR Group (Australia-based AMPYR Energy) and sells power under long-term contracts. Funding is about 420 million dollars. B2B energy services with modest brand awareness.

about: CALB (China Aviation Lithium Battery) is a Changzhou, Jiangsu maker of lithium-ion power and energy storage batteries for electric cars, buses and energy storage systems, supplying carmakers such as Xpeng, GAC, Geely and Leapmotor. It is one of China's largest battery producers and is listed in Hong Kong (3931). It had raised about 22 billion yuan in funding. A B2B supplier with low consumer brand awareness.

Farasis Energy is a Ganzhou, Jiangxi lithium battery maker supplying pouch cells and packs for electric cars, with customers including Mercedes-Benz, BAIC and Geely. It was founded in 2002 and is listed on Shanghai's STAR Market (688567). A B2B supplier with little consumer brand profile, although it has a Daimler partnership. Revenue depends on orders from carmakers, and it has expanded factories in China and Europe. It is a supplier brand with almost no consumer awareness.

TagEnergy is a Lisbon-based renewable energy company that generates and trades clean power, developing solar and wind plants in Europe and Australia and selling electricity under long-term contracts to utilities and corporate buyers. The input shows about 1.2 billion dollars raised from infrastructure investors. It is a B2B energy producer with minimal consumer brand awareness, so sponsorship fit is limited.

about: MRC Global is a Houston distributor of pipe, valves and fittings and related products for the energy and industrial sectors, serving gas utilities, downstream, upstream and industrial customers through more than 200 locations, mainly in North America. Revenue is about 3.4 billion dollars. Listed on NYSE (MRC); in 2025 it agreed to be bought by DNOW. B2B distributor with no consumer profile.

Power Corporation of Canada is a Montreal-based diversified holding company with controlling stakes in Canadian financial groups Great-West Lifeco, IGM Financial and also in Wealthsimple, and Sagard private equity. It manages about 1 trillion dollars across its businesses. Listed on the TSX (POW). Controlled by the Desmarais family. Its subsidiaries are well-known to Canadian consumers. Its units operate in Canada, the US and Europe. The group has a strong standing in Canadian business, and is a B2B investor without a consumer brand.

wiki.title: Power Corporation of Canada
wiki.text: Power Corporation of Canada (PCC) is a Canadian company founded in 1925. Initially focused on the electric utility and similar industries, it has since become a holding company with an emphasis on financial services across North America, Europe and Asia. PCC holdings include businesses in insurance, retirement services, wealth management, investment management and alternative investments.

about: Ashtrom Renewable Energy is an Israeli renewable energy developer, based in Tel Aviv, part of the Ashtrom Group, that develops, builds and operates solar and wind power plants in Israel and abroad, including in Eastern Europe and the US, selling electricity under long-term contracts. It is listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. Crunchbase lists about $470 million in funding. B2B energy producer with limited consumer brand awareness.

about: VARTA AG is a German battery maker headquartered in Ellwangen, Baden-Wurttemberg, known for micro batteries such as lithium-ion coin cells used in wireless headphones, hearing aids and wearables, and for CoinPower and V4Drive lithium-ion cells. The consumer battery division (Varta batteries sold at retail) was sold to Energizer in 2019. Listed on the Frankfurt exchange (VAR1) with a major shareholder, Porsche's investment vehicle, backing a 2024-25 restructuring. Brand awareness in Germany is high from household batteries, though now owned by Energizer.
